gaps.term: lifting the identity to d coordinates
gaps.quote: Lifting to $d$ coordinates is a tensor product: each coordinate contributes a factor $2^{2\alpha^2}$, so the factors multiply to $2^{2d\alpha^2}$.
gaps.note: The page presents the lifted identity RF_s=2^{2d\alpha^2}B_0QF_tA as following from the one-dimensional identity, but the reader cannot check how a tensor product of the transforms and permutations gives it.
